source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Checl all usb port could detect device with hot plugging.
1. Install usb key on rear USB port.
2. Boot into OS
3. Check each device can be detected under OS.
4. Check USB hot-plugging feature is workable.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Check USB device can be detected and work normally.
Replacing USB without shutting down the system.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: usbutils + operator to hot-plug the USB device
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Hot Plugging: verify USB hot-plugging (insert/remove a USB key without shutdown). Operator physically plugs/unplugs the key into the host USB ports; agent watches the OS USB event + device state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "watch -n1 'lsusb 2>&1' 2>&1 & sleep 6; kill %1; dmesg -T 2>&1 | grep -iE 'usb|new.*device|USB disconnect' | tail -20 2>&1" to confirm detect/remove. -- USB hot-plugging instance; verify detect/remove without shutdown on each rear USB port.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the dmesg USB attach/detach lines + lsusb snapshot so the user confirms the USB device was detected and removed cleanly on hot-plug; the physical plug/unplug is operator-only.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: physically hot-plugging the USB key is operator-only; agent only reads the OS USB event state.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; correctly assigns physical insertion/removal to an operator and host evidence to the agent, but relies on a timing-sensitive six-second watch and does not establish complete port or safe-removal coverage.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / IMPROVED; requires a rear-port map, approved USB identity, defined normal-operation check, synchronized events and safe unmount.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; preserves operator plug/unplug and read-only OS observation but lacks device/port identity and robust per-port evidence.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms source row 202 and the PARTIAL decision with device, port-map, normal-operation, authorization and recovery prerequisites.

original_test_intent: Verify that an approved USB key can be inserted, detected, used according to an owner-defined non-destructive criterion and safely removed without shutting down the SUT at every specified rear USB port.
original_method: With the OS running, an operator inserts the approved USB key into each rear port and later safely removes it; the OS enumeration, functional state and attach/detach evidence are recorded per port together with unexpected-log checks.
manual_activity: A qualified engineer must perform the core acceptance action by physically inserting and safely removing the approved USB key at each mapped rear port. The agent can synchronize read-only enumeration, device-event, mount and log evidence and perform only the approved non-destructive electronic check; it cannot claim the physical hot-plug was completed.
required_inputs: Exact rear USB port inventory and controller mapping
Approved non-boot USB key VID/PID/serial and data-sensitivity status
Definition of 'work normally': enumeration only or approved read/write behavior
Operator, maintenance authorization and alternate/OOB access
Safe mount/unmount/eject procedure and evidence-retention location
safety_requirements: Do not use unknown, bootable or sensitive media and do not touch boot, active input, security or management devices.
Do not remove a mounted device or one with active I/O; stop on unexpected mount, filesystem activity, overcurrent or controller error.
Preserve pre-existing logs and use timestamped before/after positions instead of clearing dmesg, syslog or SEL.
Do not retry an anomalous port automatically or generalize evidence from one port to another.
agent_execution_scope: Capture SUT identity, USB topology, device identity, mounts and baseline kernel/system/BMC evidence.
Run a continuous timestamped udev/kernel event monitor synchronized to each operator action and collect before/after enumeration.
Perform the specifically approved non-destructive usability check, correlate every result to its physical port and organize evidence without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the device, physical port matrix, functional acceptance and maintenance/recovery plan.
Perform each physical insertion and safe removal and identify the port under test.
Review per-port evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed lsusb/dmesg observations are relevant, but a six-second background watch followed by kill can miss events and neither proves clean unmount nor complete per-port coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a platform-supported continuous USB event monitor such as udevadm monitor plus timestamped lsusb/topology and mount-state captures; bind each event interval to an operator-identified port.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Rear-port hot plugging without shutdown, 5/5-minute fields and the literal normal-operation criterion are preserved; undefined functionality is requested rather than invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a port/controller matrix and capture continuous attach/detach events, exact USB identity, mount state and the approved usability check for each port; safely eject before removal and preserve all logs.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Linux hosts with udev/usbutils or equivalent OS-native USB event and inventory facilities.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS, kernel, usbutils/udev and approved USB device identity at execution time.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use the deployed OS vendor's USB enumeration/event-monitoring and safe-removal documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds synchronized per-port identity, event and mount-safety evidence without changing the physical hot-plug stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; it makes every rear port and both attach and detach observable.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Port map, approved device and exact functional criterion.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS enumeration alone cannot prove connector integrity or storage usability; a write test is prohibited unless explicitly approved for disposable media.

project_override_considerations: A project may define the rear-port subset, approved USB device and safe functional check. Engineer execution of that approved matrix means the project plan was performed; agent evidence collection must not be represented as completion of the physical hot-plug, omitted ports or an unspecified read/write criterion.
expected_evidence: SUT and OS identity, port/controller matrix, approved USB VID/PID/serial and authorization
Per-port operator timestamps plus attach/detach events, lsusb/topology and mount state
Approved non-destructive function result and safe-unmount/removal proof
Unexpected-log comparison, restored USB state, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criteria consistently require rear-port USB hot plugging without shutdown. 'Work normally' is underspecified project acceptance input, not contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The test intent and physical/automated split are clear. Missing device, port map and acceptance details are readiness gates; the core physical hot-plug requirement makes the case MANUAL ONLY rather than BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the operator boundary and relevant read-only probes but rejects both the fixed sleep/watch evidence and its PARTIAL classification because the physical action is the core stimulus.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its per-port identity, safe-removal and normal-operation safeguards but changes PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY under the locked core-physical-action rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates engineer-owned physical execution from agent evidence support, readiness, Tool Result and engineer verdict while preserving the exact rear-port scope.

review_improvement: Turns an ambiguous snapshot into a traceable per-port attach/use/detach protocol, prevents unsafe removal and avoids treating missing project selections as BLOCKED.
independent_technical_reasoning: The repeated physical plug/unplug is the stimulus being accepted, not merely setup for a later automated core. Even though electronic observation can be automated, the agent cannot perform or claim completion of that core physical operation; the correct V3.1 class is MANUAL ONLY, while missing project inputs remain readiness gates rather than BLOCKED.

source_provenance.primary: data/REVISED_commands_merged_with_raw.xlsx, Functionality row 202, read directly with openpyxl 3.1.5

no_automatic_retry: Stop and preserve evidence after any unexpected enumeration, mount, I/O, power or controller state. Repeat only after engineer diagnosis and renewed approval.
